Building a Nearest Parking App

775,502 tokens

Model 10:05 PM
Thoughts

Analyzing Bike Parking Data

I'm currently working on understanding the Singapore bike parking lot data. I've got the CSV file, and I'm parsing the information on bike parking lots with their QR codes, latitudes, and longitudes. Now, I'm thinking about the best way to calculate and return the nearest bike QR code based on a provided location.

Recommending Mobile App Structure

I'm recommending a Progressive Web App (PWA) to address their needs, since it's an excellent balance of speed and convenience. The user's GPS location is the core input, and the data will be static for each bike parking lot. A client-side nearest neighbor search using the user's location is sufficient. The output will be a quick display of the nearest bike QR code name, distance, and direction or map link.

10.1s

To build this, the most practical approach depends on whether you want a quick website (PWA) that runs on any Android browser or a native Android app.

Because your dataset contains roughly 2,500 points (~75 KB in size), you do not need a database or backend server. The entire dataset can be loaded directly onto the phone or browser, and finding the nearest location takes less than 2 milliseconds using the Haversine formula.

Option 1: Lightweight Web App / PWA (Recommended — Fastest to Build)

A web app using the HTML5 Geolocation API can be installed to your Android home screen as an app icon (PWA) and works offline.

How It Works:

  1. Convert bike_parking_lots.csv into a compact JSON array (or fetch/parse it directly).

  2. Request the user's GPS coordinates using navigator.geolocation.getCurrentPosition.

  3. Compute the distance to each parking lot using the Haversine formula.

  4. Display the closest lot name/code, distance in meters, and a "Navigate" link that opens Google Maps.

Complete Single-File Prototype (index.html):

code Html
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <meta charset="UTF-8">
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0">
  <title>Nearest Bike Parking</title>
  <style>
    body { font-family: system-ui, sans-serif; padding: 20px; text-align: center; }
    button { padding: 12px 24px; font-size: 16px; border-radius: 8px; border: none; background: #007bff; color: white; cursor: pointer; }
    .card { margin-top: 20px; padding: 16px; border: 1px solid #ddd; border-radius: 10px; display: none; }
    .code { font-size: 24px; font-weight: bold; color: #28a745; }
    .dist { font-size: 18px; color: #555; }
    a.map-btn { display: inline-block; margin-top: 12px; padding: 8px 16px; background: #28a745; color: white; text-decoration: none; border-radius: 6px; }
  </style>
</head>
<body>

  <h2>Find Nearest Bike Parking</h2>
  <button id="findBtn" onclick="findNearest()">Locate Nearest</button>
  <p id="status"></p>

  <div id="result" class="card">
    <div>Nearest Bike QR Code:</div>
    <div id="lotCode" class="code"></div>
    <div id="lotDist" class="dist"></div>
    <a id="mapLink" class="map-btn" target="_blank">Open in Google Maps</a>
  </div>

  <!-- PapaParse for parsing CSV on the fly -->
  <script src="https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/PapaParse/5.4.1/papaparse.min.js"></script>
  <script>
    let lots = [];

    // 1. Load CSV file
    fetch('bike_parking_lots.csv')
      .then(res => res.text())
      .then(csvText => {
        const parsed = Papa.parse(csvText, { header: true, dynamicTyping: true, skipEmptyLines: true });
        lots = parsed.data;
        document.getElementById('status').innerText = `Loaded ${lots.length} parking lots.`;
      });

    // 2. Haversine distance formula (in meters)
    function getDistance(lat1, lon1, lat2, lon2) {
      const R = 6371e3; // Earth radius in meters
      const φ1 = lat1 * Math.PI / 180;
      const φ2 = lat2 * Math.PI / 180;
      const Δφ = (lat2 - lat1) * Math.PI / 180;
      const Δλ = (lon2 - lon1) * Math.PI / 180;

      const a = Math.sin(Δφ / 2) ** 2 +
                Math.cos(φ1) * Math.cos(φ2) *
                Math.sin(Δλ / 2) ** 2;
      return R * 2 * Math.atan2(Math.sqrt(a), Math.sqrt(1 - a));
    }

    // 3. Get GPS Location and compute nearest
    function findNearest() {
      if (!navigator.geolocation) {
        alert("Geolocation is not supported by your browser.");
        return;
      }
      document.getElementById('status').innerText = "Acquiring GPS location...";

      navigator.geolocation.getCurrentPosition((pos) => {
        const userLat = pos.coords.latitude;
        const userLng = pos.coords.longitude;

        let nearest = null;
        let minDistance = Infinity;

        for (const lot of lots) {
          if (!lot.lat || !lot.lng) continue;
          const dist = getDistance(userLat, userLng, lot.lat, lot.lng);
          if (dist < minDistance) {
            minDistance = dist;
            nearest = lot;
          }
        }

        if (nearest) {
          document.getElementById('status').innerText = "";
          document.getElementById('lotCode').innerText = nearest.name;
          document.getElementById('lotDist').innerText = `${Math.round(minDistance)} meters away`;
          document.getElementById('mapLink').href = `https://www.google.com/maps/dir/?api=1&destination=${nearest.lat},${nearest.lng}`;
          document.getElementById('result').style.display = 'block';
        }
      }, (err) => {
        document.getElementById('status').innerText = "Error: " + err.message;
      }, { enableHighAccuracy: true });
    }
  </script>
</body>
</html>

  • Deployment: Drop index.html and bike_parking_lots.csv into a repository on GitHub Pages, Vercel, or Cloudflare Pages for free.

Option 2: Native Android App (Kotlin)

If you need deeper Android integration (e.g., home-screen widgets, background location tracking, or built-in QR scanner):

1. Setup & Permissions

In AndroidManifest.xml, request location permissions:

code Xml
<uses-permission android:name="android.permission.ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION" />
<uses-permission android:name="android.permission.ACCESS_COARSE_LOCATION" />

Add Google Play Services Location dependency in build.gradle:

code Groovy
implementation 'com.google.android.gms:play-services-location:21.1.0'

2. Store the Data

Place bike_parking_lots.csv in your app's app/src/main/assets/ directory.

3. Core Search Logic (Kotlin)

code Kotlin
data class ParkingLot(val name: String, val lat: Double, val lng: Double)

fun loadParkingLots(context: Context): List<ParkingLot> {
    val lots = mutableListOf<ParkingLot>()
    context.assets.open("bike_parking_lots.csv").bufferedReader().useLines { lines ->
        lines.drop(1).forEach { line ->
            val tokens = line.split(",")
            if (tokens.size >= 3) {
                val name = tokens[0]
                val lat = tokens[1].toDoubleOrNull()
                val lng = tokens[2].toDoubleOrNull()
                if (lat != null && lng != null) {
                    lots.add(ParkingLot(name, lat, lng))
                }
            }
        }
    }
    return lots
}

fun findNearestLot(userLocation: Location, lots: List<ParkingLot>): Pair<ParkingLot, Float>? {
    var nearestLot: ParkingLot? = null
    var minDistance = Float.MAX_VALUE

    val lotLocation = Location("")
    for (lot in lots) {
        lotLocation.latitude = lot.lat
        lotLocation.longitude = lot.lng
        
        val distance = userLocation.distanceTo(lotLocation) // Built-in Haversine in meters
        if (distance < minDistance) {
            minDistance = distance
            nearestLot = lot
        }
    }
    return nearestLot?.let { it to minDistance }
}

4. Getting Location:

Use FusedLocationProviderClient:

code Kotlin
val fusedLocationClient = LocationServices.getFusedLocationProviderClient(context)
fusedLocationClient.getCurrentLocation(Priority.PRIORITY_HIGH_ACCURACY, null)
    .addOnSuccessListener { location: Location? ->
        if (location != null) {
            val result = findNearestLot(location, lots)
            val nearest = result?.first
            val distance = result?.second
            // Update UI with nearest.name and distance
        }
    }

Option 3: Native Android App (Kotlin)

If building a native Android app, you don't have to worry about CORS.

1. Add Dependencies (app/build.gradle)

code Groovy
implementation 'com.google.android.gms:play-services-location:21.1.0'
implementation 'com.squareup.okhttp3:okhttp:4.12.0'
implementation 'com.google.code.gson:gson:2.10.1'

2. Request & Fetch Logic (Kotlin)

code Kotlin
import android.location.Location
import com.google.android.gms.location.LocationServices
import com.google.android.gms.location.Priority
import com.google.gson.Gson
import okhttp3.OkHttpClient
import okhttp3.Request
import kotlin.concurrent.thread

data class ParkingResponse(
    val id: String,
    val distanceMeters: Double
)

fun fetchNearestBikeLot(context: Context, onResult: (ParkingResponse?) -> Unit) {
    val fusedClient = LocationServices.getFusedLocationProviderClient(context)
    val client = OkHttpClient()

    fusedClient.getCurrentLocation(Priority.PRIORITY_HIGH_ACCURACY, null)
        .addOnSuccessListener { location: Location? ->
            if (location != null) {
                thread {
                    val url = "https://mingjun.dev/bike-parking/?lat=${location.latitude}&lng=${location.longitude}"
                    val request = Request.Builder().url(url).build()

                    try {
                        val response = client.newCall(request).execute()
                        val json = response.body?.string()
                        val result = Gson().fromJson(json, ParkingResponse::class.java)
                        onResult(result)
                    } catch (e: Exception) {
                        e.printStackTrace()
                        onResult(null)
                    }
                }
            }
        }
}

A Quick Architecture Tip

ApproachProsCons
Using the API (mingjun.dev)Zero dataset to maintain, tiny code footprint.Fails if you have poor cell signal (common around sheltered/underground bike racks) or if the personal domain goes offline.
Local Offline Calculation (Client-side)100% reliable, instant (0ms latency), works without internet.Must store the ~75KB dataset locally.

Recommendation: If you want the most reliable experience, consider using the API as the primary source, but keeping the CSV in your app as an offline fallback.

Yes, absolutely.

You have two main ways to display your location and the bike stop on a map inside a web app:

Option A: OpenStreetMap + Leaflet.js (Recommended)

Why it's usually preferred for web apps:

  • 100% free with no API key or credit card needed (Google Maps Embed/JS API requires a Google Cloud project with billing enabled).

  • Allows you to show both markers simultaneously (a blue dot for you, a green pin for the bike rack) and auto-zooms to fit both.

  • You can still include an "Open in Google Maps" button that launches the native Google Maps navigation app on your Android phone.

Complete Ready-to-Run Single-File Demo:

Save this as index.html:

code Html
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <meta charset="UTF-8">
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0">
  <title>Nearest Bike Parking</title>

  <!-- Leaflet CSS for Map Styling -->
  <link rel="stylesheet" href="https://unpkg.com/leaflet@1.9.4/dist/leaflet.css" />

  <style>
    body { font-family: system-ui, sans-serif; margin: 0; padding: 16px; text-align: center; }
    button { padding: 12px 24px; font-size: 16px; border-radius: 8px; border: none; background: #007bff; color: white; cursor: pointer; }
    .card { margin: 15px auto; padding: 12px; border: 1px solid #ddd; border-radius: 8px; max-width: 450px; display: none; }
    .code { font-size: 22px; font-weight: bold; color: #28a745; }
    #map { height: 350px; width: 100%; max-width: 450px; margin: 15px auto; border-radius: 8px; display: none; }
    .nav-btn { display: inline-block; margin-top: 10px; padding: 8px 16px; background: #34a853; color: white; text-decoration: none; border-radius: 6px; font-size: 14px; }
  </style>
</head>
<body>

  <h2>Nearest Bike Parking Spot</h2>
  <button id="locateBtn" onclick="findAndShow()">Locate Nearest</button>
  <p id="status"></p>

  <div id="result" class="card">
    <div>Nearest QR Code ID:</div>
    <div id="qrId" class="code"></div>
    <div id="distance"></div>
    <a id="gmapsLink" class="nav-btn" target="_blank">Open Navigation in Google Maps</a>
  </div>

  <!-- Embedded Map Container -->
  <div id="map"></div>

  <!-- Leaflet JS -->
  <script src="https://unpkg.com/leaflet@1.9.4/dist/leaflet.js"></script>
  <script>
    let map = null;

    function findAndShow() {
      const status = document.getElementById('status');
      status.innerText = "Acquiring GPS location...";

      navigator.geolocation.getCurrentPosition(async (pos) => {
        const userLat = pos.coords.latitude;
        const userLng = pos.coords.longitude;

        status.innerText = "Finding nearest parking spot...";

        try {
          const res = await fetch(`https://mingjun.dev/bike-parking/?lat=${userLat}&lng=${userLng}`);
          const data = await res.json();

          const destLat = data.location.lat;
          const destLng = data.location.lng;

          // 1. Update text details
          document.getElementById('qrId').innerText = data.id;
          document.getElementById('distance').innerText = `${Math.round(data.distanceMeters)}m away`;
          document.getElementById('gmapsLink').href = `https://www.google.com/maps/dir/?api=1&destination=${destLat},${destLng}&travelmode=walking`;
          
          document.getElementById('result').style.display = 'block';
          document.getElementById('map').style.display = 'block';
          status.innerText = "";

          // 2. Initialize or update Leaflet Map
          if (!map) {
            map = L.map('map');
            L.tileLayer('https://{s}.tile.openstreetmap.org/{z}/{x}/{y}.png', {
              maxZoom: 19,
              attribution: '© OpenStreetMap'
            }).addTo(map);
          }

          // Clear any previous markers
          map.eachLayer((layer) => {
            if (layer instanceof L.Marker || layer instanceof L.CircleMarker) {
              map.removeLayer(layer);
            }
          });

          // 3. Add User Marker (Blue Dot)
          L.circleMarker([userLat, userLng], {
            radius: 8,
            color: '#007bff',
            fillColor: '#007bff',
            fillOpacity: 0.9
          }).addTo(map).bindPopup("You are here").openPopup();

          // 4. Add Destination Marker (Bike Spot)
          L.marker([destLat, destLng]).addTo(map)
            .bindPopup(`<b>${data.id}</b><br>${Math.round(data.distanceMeters)}m away`);

          // 5. Fit map view to show both points with padding
          map.fitBounds([
            [userLat, userLng],
            [destLat, destLng]
          ], { padding: [40, 40] });

        } catch (err) {
          status.innerText = "Error fetching bike spot: " + err.message;
        }
      }, (err) => {
        status.innerText = "GPS Error: " + err.message;
      }, { enableHighAccuracy: true });
    }
  </script>
</body>
</html>

Comparison:

  • Option A (Leaflet/OpenStreetMap): Fully customizable, allows adding multiple bike parking spots around you, lets you style pins, and is completely free with no API quota limits.

  • Option B (Google Maps iframe): Uses familiar Google Maps imagery and shows turn-by-turn walking route lines, but Google's free embed iframe can sometimes enforce cookies/captchas or rate-limit automated requests.

Yes, it is very feasible and is the standard way to build location-based apps on Android[1].

Google provides the official Maps SDK for Android, which renders smooth, interactive vector maps directly inside your app UI[1].

Why It’s Great on Android

  1. Free for Native Mobile: Unlike Google Maps on the web (which charges after a monthly quota), standard dynamic map loads using the Maps SDK for Android are free and unlimited for mobile applications[2][3].

  2. Built-in "My Location" Layer: Android handles your current location dot, direction compass, and "re-center" button automatically with just one line of code: googleMap.isMyLocationEnabled = true.

  3. Smooth Performance: Native 60 FPS hardware acceleration, gesture zooming, tilt, and offline tile caching.

How to Implement It (Step-by-Step)

1. Get an API Key (Google Cloud Console)

  1. Go to the Google Cloud Console and create a project.

  2. Enable Maps SDK for Android[1].

  3. Create an API Key and restrict it to your app’s Package Name and SHA-1 fingerprint (for security).

2. Add Dependencies (app/build.gradle)

code Groovy
dependencies {
    // Google Maps & Location services
    implementation 'com.google.android.gms:play-services-maps:18.2.0'
    implementation 'com.google.android.gms:play-services-location:21.1.0'
}

3. Update AndroidManifest.xml

Add your permissions and API key:

code Xml
<manifest ...>
    <!-- Location Permissions -->
    <uses-permission android:name="android.permission.ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION" />
    <uses-permission android:name="android.permission.ACCESS_COARSE_LOCATION" />

    <application ...>
        <!-- Put your Google Maps API Key here -->
        <meta-data
            android:name="com.google.android.geo.API_KEY"
            android:value="YOUR_API_KEY_HERE" />
    </application>
</manifest>

4. Add the Map to Layout (activity_main.xml)

code Xml
<fragment
    android:id="@+id/mapFragment"
    android:name="com.google.android.gms.maps.SupportMapFragment"
    android:layout_width="match_parent"
    android:layout_height="match_parent" />

5. Kotlin Implementation (MainActivity.kt)

This handles fetching the nearest spot (using the API or local calculation), plotting both your position and the bike parking marker, and auto-framing the camera so both are visible:

code Kotlin
import android.Manifest
import android.content.pm.PackageManager
import android.os.Bundle
import androidx.appcompat.app.AppCompatActivity
import androidx.core.app.ActivityCompat
import com.google.android.gms.location.LocationServices
import com.google.android.gms.location.Priority
import com.google.android.gms.maps.CameraUpdateFactory
import com.google.android.gms.maps.GoogleMap
import com.google.android.gms.maps.OnMapReadyCallback
import com.google.android.gms.maps.SupportMapFragment
import com.google.android.gms.maps.model.BitmapDescriptorFactory
import com.google.android.gms.maps.model.LatLng
import com.google.android.gms.maps.model.LatLngBounds
import com.google.android.gms.maps.model.MarkerOptions

class MainActivity : AppCompatActivity(), OnMapReadyCallback {

    private lateinit var mMap: GoogleMap

    override fun onCreate(savedInstanceState: Bundle?) {
        super.onCreate(savedInstanceState)
        setContentView(R.layout.activity_main)

        val mapFragment = supportFragmentManager.findFragmentById(R.id.mapFragment) as SupportMapFragment
        mapFragment.getMapAsync(this)
    }

    override fun onMapReady(googleMap: GoogleMap) {
        mMap = googleMap

        // 1. Check Location Permission
        if (ActivityCompat.checkSelfPermission(this, Manifest.permission.ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION) != PackageManager.PERMISSION_GRANTED) {
            ActivityCompat.requestPermissions(this, arrayOf(Manifest.permission.ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION), 1001)
            return
        }

        // 2. Enable the default Google Maps blue pulsing location dot
        mMap.isMyLocationEnabled = true

        // 3. Get Current Location & plot the nearest spot
        val fusedLocationClient = LocationServices.getFusedLocationProviderClient(this)
        fusedLocationClient.getCurrentLocation(Priority.PRIORITY_HIGH_ACCURACY, null)
            .addOnSuccessListener { location ->
                if (location != null) {
                    val userLatLng = LatLng(location.latitude, location.longitude)
                    
                    // Example destination coordinates (e.g., from the API result: MRS-0003)
                    val bikeSpotId = "MRS-0003"
                    val bikeSpotLatLng = LatLng(1.280074, 103.870828)

                    // 4. Add a pin for the bike parking spot
                    mMap.addMarker(
                        MarkerOptions()
                            .position(bikeSpotLatLng)
                            .title(bikeSpotId)
                            .snippet("Nearest bike parking")
                            .icon(BitmapDescriptorFactory.defaultMarker(BitmapDescriptorFactory.HUE_GREEN))
                    )?.showInfoWindow()

                    // 5. Auto-zoom to show both user and parking spot together
                    val bounds = LatLngBounds.builder()
                        .include(userLatLng)
                        .include(bikeSpotLatLng)
                        .build()

                    mMap.animateCamera(CameraUpdateFactory.newLatLngBounds(bounds, 150))
                }
            }
    }
}

GitHub Pages is ideal for this project. The browser’s Geolocation API strictly requires an HTTPS connection to work on mobile, and GitHub Pages provides free HTTPS out of the box.

Step 1: Prepare Your index.html File

Create a file named index.html on your computer. Below is the complete code containing the API fetch, Leaflet map embed (blue dot for you, green pin for the bike spot), and a 1-tap Google Maps walking navigation button:

code Html
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <meta charset="UTF-8" />
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0, maximum-scale=1.0, user-scalable=no" />
  <title>Nearest Bike Parking</title>

  <!-- Leaflet Map CSS -->
  <link rel="stylesheet" href="https://unpkg.com/leaflet@1.9.4/dist/leaflet.css" />

  <style>
    * { box-sizing: border-box; }
    body {
      font-family: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "Segoe UI", Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif;
      margin: 0; padding: 16px; text-align: center; background: #f8f9fa; color: #333;
    }
    h2 { margin-top: 10px; font-size: 22px; }
    .btn {
      width: 100%; max-width: 400px; padding: 14px; font-size: 16px; font-weight: bold;
      border-radius: 10px; border: none; background: #007bff; color: white; cursor: pointer;
      box-shadow: 0 4px 6px rgba(0,123,255,0.2);
    }
    .btn:active { transform: scale(0.98); }
    #status { margin: 12px 0; font-size: 14px; color: #666; }
    .card {
      margin: 15px auto; padding: 16px; border-radius: 12px; background: white;
      box-shadow: 0 2px 8px rgba(0,0,0,0.08); max-width: 400px; display: none;
    }
    .code { font-size: 28px; font-weight: 800; color: #28a745; letter-spacing: 1px; }
    .distance { font-size: 16px; color: #666; margin: 4px 0 14px 0; }
    .nav-btn {
      display: block; width: 100%; padding: 10px; background: #28a745; color: white;
      text-decoration: none; border-radius: 8px; font-weight: 600; font-size: 15px;
    }
    #map {
      height: 320px; width: 100%; max-width: 400px; margin: 15px auto;
      border-radius: 12px; display: none; box-shadow: 0 2px 8px rgba(0,0,0,0.08);
    }
  </style>
</head>
<body>

  <h2>🚲 Find Nearest Bike QR</h2>
  <button class="btn" onclick="findNearest()">Locate Nearest Parking</button>
  <div id="status">Tap the button to find the nearest bike stop.</div>

  <div id="result" class="card">
    <div style="font-size: 13px; text-transform: uppercase; color: #888;">Nearest QR ID</div>
    <div id="qrId" class="code">-</div>
    <div id="dist" class="distance">-</div>
    <a id="navLink" class="nav-btn" target="_blank">Navigate in Google Maps</a>
  </div>

  <div id="map"></div>

  <!-- Leaflet Map JS -->
  <script src="https://unpkg.com/leaflet@1.9.4/dist/leaflet.js"></script>
  <script>
    let map = null;

    function findNearest() {
      const status = document.getElementById('status');
      if (!navigator.geolocation) {
        status.innerText = "Geolocation not supported by your browser.";
        return;
      }

      status.innerText = "Acquiring GPS location...";

      navigator.geolocation.getCurrentPosition(async (pos) => {
        const userLat = pos.coords.latitude;
        const userLng = pos.coords.longitude;
        status.innerText = "Searching for closest parking lot...";

        try {
          const res = await fetch(`https://mingjun.dev/bike-parking/?lat=${userLat}&lng=${userLng}`);
          const data = await res.json();

          const destLat = data.location.lat;
          const destLng = data.location.lng;

          // Update Info Card
          document.getElementById('qrId').innerText = data.id;
          document.getElementById('dist').innerText = `${Math.round(data.distanceMeters)} meters away`;
          document.getElementById('navLink').href = 
            `https://www.google.com/maps/dir/?api=1&destination=${destLat},${destLng}&travelmode=walking`;
          
          document.getElementById('result').style.display = 'block';
          document.getElementById('map').style.display = 'block';
          status.innerText = "";

          // Render / Update Leaflet Map
          if (!map) {
            map = L.map('map');
            L.tileLayer('https://{s}.tile.openstreetmap.org/{z}/{x}/{y}.png', {
              maxZoom: 19,
              attribution: '© OpenStreetMap'
            }).addTo(map);
          }

          // Clear prior markers
          map.eachLayer((layer) => {
            if (layer instanceof L.Marker || layer instanceof L.CircleMarker) {
              map.removeLayer(layer);
            }
          });

          // Blue marker for user
          L.circleMarker([userLat, userLng], {
            radius: 8,
            color: '#007bff',
            fillColor: '#007bff',
            fillOpacity: 0.9
          }).addTo(map).bindPopup("You are here");

          // Green marker for destination bike spot
          L.marker([destLat, destLng]).addTo(map)
            .bindPopup(`<b>${data.id}</b><br>${Math.round(data.distanceMeters)}m away`)
            .openPopup();

          // Auto-zoom to show both user and bike stop
          map.fitBounds([
            [userLat, userLng],
            [destLat, destLng]
          ], { padding: [40, 40] });

        } catch (err) {
          status.innerText = "Failed to fetch: " + err.message;
        }
      }, (err) => {
        status.innerText = "GPS Error: " + err.message;
      }, { enableHighAccuracy: true });
    }
  </script>
</body>
</html>

Step 2: Create a GitHub Repository

  1. Go to GitHub.com and log in.

  2. In the top-right corner, click + → New repository.

  3. Choose a repository name (e.g., bike-parking).

  4. Set it to Public (GitHub Pages requires public repos on free accounts).

  5. Leave the checkboxes empty and click Create repository.

Step 3: Upload Your File

Option A: Using GitHub's Website Directly (Easiest)

  1. On your newly created repository page, click uploading an existing file.

  2. Drag and drop your index.html file into the box.

  3. Scroll down and click the green Commit changes button.

Option B: Using Git Command Line

code Bash
git init
git add index.html
git commit -m "Initial commit"
git branch -M main
git remote add origin https://github.com/<YOUR-USERNAME>/bike-parking.git
git push -u origin main

Step 4: Enable GitHub Pages

  1. In your repository, click the Settings tab at the top.

  2. In the left sidebar, click Pages (under the "Code and automation" section).

  3. Under Build and deployment → Branch:

    • Change None to main (or master).

    • Leave the folder as / (root).

    • Click Save.

  4. Wait about 30–60 seconds, then refresh the page.

  5. At the top of the Pages section, you will see a banner with your live URL:

    code Code
    https://<YOUR-USERNAME>.github.io/bike-parking/

Step 5: Test and Install on Android

  1. Open Chrome on your Android phone and navigate to your GitHub Pages URL.

  2. Tap the button and grant Location Access when prompted by Chrome.

  3. Turn it into an app icon: Tap the three dots menu (⋮) in Chrome and select "Add to Home screen" or "Install app". It will place an icon on your home screen so you can open it anytime with a single tap.

Analyzing the Fetch Error

I'm now focusing on the root causes of the "Failed to fetch" error. It appears the issue stems from CORS restrictions, because mingjun.dev lacks the necessary Access-Control-Allow-Origin headers. Alternatively, a mixed content scenario might be present if the page is using HTTP.

Evaluating Offline Solutions

I've been exploring a complete solution: embedding the dataset directly. This approach eliminates CORS issues entirely, ensuring offline functionality and instant nearest parking lot calculations. The small size of the dataset makes this a feasible and reliable option, providing identical results as the original setup. Relying on a third-party server becomes unnecessary, so the web app's reliability increases dramatically.

That error happens because of CORS (Cross-Origin Resource Sharing).

Web browsers block your page on GitHub Pages from reading data from mingjun.dev because that server doesn't include the header (Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *) that permits other websites to access it.

Solution 1: Host the CSV in your repo (Recommended — 100% Reliable & Offline-Ready)

Instead of calling an external server that blocks browser requests, upload the bike_parking_lots.csv file you provided earlier to the same GitHub repository.

Because index.html and bike_parking_lots.csv are hosted on the same domain, there are zero CORS errors, zero network latency, and it will work forever even without an external API.

1. In your GitHub repository:

Upload your bike_parking_lots.csv file into the repository root alongside index.html.

2. Replace your index.html with this code:

code Html
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <meta charset="UTF-8" />
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0, maximum-scale=1.0, user-scalable=no" />
  <title>Nearest Bike Parking</title>

  <!-- Leaflet Map CSS -->
  <link rel="stylesheet" href="https://unpkg.com/leaflet@1.9.4/dist/leaflet.css" />

  <style>
    * { box-sizing: border-box; }
    body {
      font-family: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "Segoe UI", Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif;
      margin: 0; padding: 16px; text-align: center; background: #f8f9fa; color: #333;

    }

    #status { margin: 12px 0; font-size: 14px; color: #666; }
    .card {
      margin: 15px auto; padding: 16px; border-radius: 12px; background: white;
      box-shadow: 0 2px 8px rgba(0,0,0,0.08); max-width: 400px; display: none;
    }
    .code { font-size: 28px; font-weight: 800; color: #28a745; letter-spacing: 1px; }
    .distance { font-size: 16px; color: #666; margin: 4px 0 14px 0; }
    .nav-btn {
      display: block; width: 100%; padding: 10px; background: #28a745; color: white;
      text-decoration: none; border-radius: 8px; font-weight: 600; font-size: 15px;
    }
    #map {
      height: 320px; width: 100%; max-width: 400px; margin: 15px auto;
      border-radius: 12px; display: none; box-shadow: 0 2px 8px rgba(0,0,0,0.08);
    }
  </style>
</head>
<body>

  <h2>🚲 Find Nearest Bike QR</h2>
  <button class="btn" id="actionBtn" onclick="findNearest()">Locate Nearest Parking</button>
  <div id="status">Loading parking spots database...</div>

  <div id="result" class="card">
    <div style="font-size: 13px; text-transform: uppercase; color: #888;">Nearest QR ID</div>
    <div id="qrId" class="code">-</div>
    <div id="dist" class="distance">-</div>
    <a id="navLink" class="nav-btn" target="_blank">Navigate in Google Maps</a>
  </div>

  <div id="map"></div>

  <!-- PapaParse for parsing the CSV & Leaflet for the Map -->
  <script src="https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/PapaParse/5.4.1/papaparse.min.js"></script>
  <script src="https://unpkg.com/leaflet@1.9.4/dist/leaflet.js"></script>

  <script>
    let parkingLots = [];
    let map = null;

    // Load CSV file locally from the same GitHub repo (Zero CORS issues)
    fetch('./bike_parking_lots.csv')
      .then(res => {
        if (!res.ok) throw new Error("Could not find bike_parking_lots.csv");
        return res.text();
      })
      .then(csvText => {
        const parsed = Papa.parse(csvText, { header: true, dynamicTyping: true, skipEmptyLines: true });
        parkingLots = parsed.data;
        document.getElementById('status').innerText = `Ready! Loaded ${parkingLots.length} parking spots.`;
      })
      .catch(err => {
        document.getElementById('status').innerText = "Error: " + err.message;
      });

    // Haversine distance formula in meters
    function getDistance(lat1, lon1, lat2, lon2) {
      const R = 6371e3;
      const dLat = (lat2 - lat1) * Math.PI / 180;
      const dLon = (lon2 - lon1) * Math.PI / 180;
      const a = Math.sin(dLat / 2) ** 2 +
                Math.cos(lat1 * Math.PI / 180) * Math.cos(lat2 * Math.PI / 180) *
                Math.sin(dLon / 2) ** 2;
      return R * 2 * Math.atan2(Math.sqrt(a), Math.sqrt(1 - a));
    }

    function findNearest() {
      const status = document.getElementById('status');

      if (parkingLots.length === 0) {
        status.innerText = "Still loading parking lots, please wait...";
        return;
      }

      status.innerText = "Acquiring GPS location...";

      navigator.geolocation.getCurrentPosition((pos) => {
        const userLat = pos.coords.latitude;
        const userLng = pos.coords.longitude;

        let closest = null;
        let minDistance = Infinity;

        // Iterate through all spots (~2ms calculation time)
        for (const spot of parkingLots) {
          if (!spot.lat || !spot.lng) continue;
          const dist = getDistance(userLat, userLng, spot.lat, spot.lng);
          if (dist < minDistance) {
            minDistance = dist;
            closest = spot;
          }
        }

        if (!closest) {
          status.innerText = "No parking spots found.";
          return;
        }

        // Update UI
        document.getElementById('qrId').innerText = closest.name;
        document.getElementById('dist').innerText = `${Math.round(minDistance)} meters away`;
        document.getElementById('navLink').href = 
          `https://www.google.com/maps/dir/?api=1&destination=${closest.lat},${closest.lng}&travelmode=walking`;

        document.getElementById('result').style.display = 'block';
        document.getElementById('map').style.display = 'block';
        status.innerText = "";

        // Render Leaflet Map
        if (!map) {
          map = L.map('map');
          L.tileLayer('https://{s}.tile.openstreetmap.org/{z}/{x}/{y}.png', {
            maxZoom: 19,
            attribution: '© OpenStreetMap'
          }).addTo(map);
        }

        map.eachLayer((layer) => {
          if (layer instanceof L.Marker || layer instanceof L.CircleMarker) {
            map.removeLayer(layer);
          }
        });

        // User location marker (Blue circle)
        L.circleMarker([userLat, userLng], {
          radius: 8,
          color: '#007bff',
          fillColor: '#007bff',
          fillOpacity: 0.9
        }).addTo(map).bindPopup("You are here");

        // Nearest parking lot marker
        L.marker([closest.lat, closest.lng]).addTo(map)
          .bindPopup(`<b>${closest.name}</b><br>${Math.round(minDistance)}m away`)
          .openPopup();

        // Fit map view to both points
        map.fitBounds([
          [userLat, userLng],
          [closest.lat, closest.lng]
        ], { padding: [40, 40] });

      }, (err) => {
        status.innerText = "GPS Error: " + err.message;
      }, { enableHighAccuracy: true });
    }
  </script>
</body>
</html>

Solution 2: Quick CORS Proxy (If you prefer using the API)

If you strictly want to use mingjun.dev without uploading the CSV, route the request through a free CORS proxy like corsproxy.io:

Change this line in your original code:

code JavaScript
const res = await fetch(`https://mingjun.dev/bike-parking/?lat=${userLat}&lng=${userLng}`);

To this:

code JavaScript
const apiUrl = encodeURIComponent(`https://mingjun.dev/bike-parking/?lat=${userLat}&lng=${userLng}`);
const res = await fetch(`https://corsproxy.io/?${apiUrl}`);

Solution 1 is recommended because public CORS proxies can occasionally be blocked or go down, whereas hosting the CSV file in your own repo ensures your web app works every time.

    function copyCode(text, btn) {
      navigator.clipboard.writeText(text).then(() => {
        const prevText = btn.innerText;
        btn.innerText = "Copied! ✓";
        btn.classList.add("copied");
        setTimeout(() => {
          btn.innerText = prevText;
          btn.classList.remove("copied");
        }, 1500);
      }).catch(err => {
        alert("Copy failed: " + err);
      });
    }

    function findNearest() {
      const status = document.getElementById('status');

      if (parkingLots.length === 0) {
        status.innerText = "Still loading parking lots, please wait...";
        return;
      }

      status.innerText = "Acquiring GPS location...";

      navigator.geolocation.getCurrentPosition((pos) => {
        const userLat = pos.coords.latitude;
        const userLng = pos.coords.longitude;

        status.innerText = "Calculating distances...";

        // 1. Calculate distances to all spots
        const withDistances = parkingLots.map(spot => ({
          ...spot,
          distance: getDistance(userLat, userLng, spot.lat, spot.lng)
        }));

        // 2. Sort ascending and pick the top 5
        withDistances.sort((a, b) => a.distance - b.distance);
        const top5 = withDistances.slice(0, 5);

        // 3. Render Top 5 Cards
        const listDiv = document.getElementById('spotsList');
        listDiv.innerHTML = "";

        top5.forEach((spot, idx) => {
          const isFirst = idx === 0;
          const card = document.createElement('div');
          card.className = `spot-card ${isFirst ? 'closest' : ''}`;
          card.innerHTML = `
            <div class="spot-info">
              <span class="spot-rank">${isFirst ? '★ CLOSEST' : '#' + (idx + 1)}</span>
              <div class="spot-code">${spot.name}</div>
              <div class="spot-dist">${Math.round(spot.distance)} meters away</div>
            </div>
            <div class="spot-actions">
              <button class="btn-copy" onclick="copyCode('${spot.name}', this)">Copy ID</button>
              <a class="btn-nav" target="_blank" href="https://www.google.com/maps/dir/?api=1&destination=${spot.lat},${spot.lng}&travelmode=walking">Go ➔</a>
            </div>
          `;
          listDiv.appendChild(card);
        });

        document.getElementById('resultsContainer').style.display = 'block';
        document.getElementById('map').style.display = 'block';
        status.innerText = "";

        // 4. Initialize / Update Leaflet Map
        if (!map) {
          map = L.map('map');
          L.tileLayer('https://{s}.tile.openstreetmap.org/{z}/{x}/{y}.png', {
            maxZoom: 19,
            attribution: '© OpenStreetMap'
          }).addTo(map);
        }

        // Clear existing markers
        map.eachLayer((layer) => {
          if (layer instanceof L.Marker || layer instanceof L.CircleMarker) {
            map.removeLayer(layer);
          }
        });

        const bounds = [[userLat, userLng]];

        // User Marker (Blue Dot)
        L.circleMarker([userLat, userLng], {
          radius: 8,
          color: '#007bff',
          fillColor: '#007bff',
          fillOpacity: 0.9
        }).addTo(map).bindPopup("<b>You are here</b>");

        // Plot all 5 markers on the map
        top5.forEach((spot, idx) => {
          bounds.push([spot.lat, spot.lng]);
          const marker = L.marker([spot.lat, spot.lng]).addTo(map);
          marker.bindPopup(`<b>#${idx + 1}: ${spot.name}</b><br>${Math.round(spot.distance)}m away`);
          
          if (idx === 0) {
            marker.openPopup(); // Pop up the closest one by default
          }
        });

        // Frame all points on screen
        map.fitBounds(bounds, { padding: [30, 30] });

      }, (err) => {
        status.innerText = "GPS Error: " + err.message;
      }, { enableHighAccuracy: true });
    }
  </script>
</body>
</html>

Commit and push this change to your repository. Refresh your GitHub Pages URL on your Android phone, and you will see the full top 5 list with instant copy buttons and all markers plotted on the map.

Chrome on Android only allows installing a website as an app if it qualifies as a Progressive Web App (PWA).

To make it installable, Chrome requires three things:

  1. A manifest.json file describing the app name and settings.

  2. Two PNG icons (192x192 and 512x512).

  3. A Service Worker (sw.js) registered in the background.

  4. Correct relative paths (a common GitHub Pages trap: setting the start URL to / instead of ./ fails because GitHub Pages lives in a subfolder like /bike-parking/).

Follow these steps to fix it:

Step 1: Create manifest.json

Create a new file named manifest.json in the root of your GitHub repository:

code JSON
{
  "name": "Nearest Bike Parking",
  "short_name": "BikeQR",
  "description": "Find the nearest bicycle parking lot QR code in Singapore",
  "start_url": "./",
  "scope": "./",
  "display": "standalone",
  "background_color": "#f4f6f8",
  "theme_color": "#007bff",
  "orientation": "portrait",
  "icons": [
    {
      "src": "icon-192.png",
      "sizes": "192x192",
      "type": "image/png",
      "purpose": "any maskable"
    },
    {
      "src": "icon-512.png",
      "sizes": "512x512",
      "type": "image/png",
      "purpose": "any maskable"
    }
  ]
}

Step 2: Add the Two App Icons

Chrome strictly requires 192×192 and 512×512 PNG icons.

You need two image files in the root of your repo named:

  • icon-192.png

  • icon-512.png

Quick way to generate them:

  1. Go to any free icon generator like favicon.io/favicon-generator/ or app-manifest.firebaseapp.com.

  2. Pick a bicycle emoji (🚲), choose a blue background, and generate the package.

  3. Rename the generated android-chrome-192x192.png to icon-192.png and the 512x512 one to icon-512.png, then upload both to your repository.

Step 3: Create sw.js (Service Worker)

Create a file named sw.js in the root of your repository. This tells Chrome the app can cache assets and run standalone:

code JavaScript
const CACHE_NAME = 'bike-parking-v1';
const ASSETS_TO_CACHE = [
  './',
  './index.html',
  './bike_parking_lots.csv',
  './manifest.json',
  './icon-192.png',
  './icon-512.png'
];

self.addEventListener('install', (event) => {
  event.waitUntil(
    caches.open(CACHE_NAME).then((cache) => {
      return cache.addAll(ASSETS_TO_CACHE);
    })
  );
  self.skipWaiting();
});

self.addEventListener('activate', (event) => {
  event.waitUntil(
    caches.keys().then((keys) => {
      return Promise.all(
        keys.map((key) => {
          if (key !== CACHE_NAME) return caches.delete(key);
        })
      );
    })
  );
  self.clients.claim();
});

self.addEventListener('fetch', (event) => {
  event.respondWith(
    caches.match(event.request).then((cachedResponse) => {
      return cachedResponse || fetch(event.request);
    })
  );
});

Step 4: Link Everything in index.html

In your existing index.html, make two small additions:

1. In the <head> section:

Add the manifest and theme color tags:

code Html
<link rel="manifest" href="./manifest.json" />
<meta name="theme-color" content="#007bff" />
<link rel="apple-touch-icon" href="icon-192.png" />

2. Inside the <script> section (at the bottom):

Add the service worker registration:

code JavaScript
// Register Service Worker for PWA installation
if ('serviceWorker' in navigator) {
  window.addEventListener('load', () => {
    navigator.serviceWorker.register('./sw.js')
      .then(reg => console.log('Service Worker registered', reg))
      .catch(err => console.log('Service Worker registration failed', err));
  });
}

Final Repository File Structure

Your GitHub repository should now look like this:

code Text
your-repo/
├── bike_parking_lots.csv
├── icon-192.png
├── icon-512.png
├── index.html
├── manifest.json
└── sw.js

How to Install on Android:

  1. Commit and push all files to GitHub.

  2. Wait 1 minute for GitHub Pages to rebuild.

  3. Open the link in Chrome on your phone.

  4. Hard refresh the page (or clear site cache) so Chrome discovers the new service worker.

  5. Tap Chrome's three dots (⋮) menu — you will now see "Install app" (or "Add to Home screen" with an app badge), and it will install with the custom icon and open without browser address bars.

If the page stays stuck on "Loading parking spots database..." without showing an error, it means the JavaScript stopped executing before the fetch could complete.

This almost always happens because of one of two things:

  1. The Service Worker (sw.js) crashed during install: If icon-192.png or icon-512.png hasn't been uploaded yet, cache.addAll() crashes and leaves the page in a broken cached state.

  2. The external parser CDN (PapaParse) stalled or was blocked on your mobile network.

Step 1: Clear the Broken Cache in Chrome (Do this on your phone first)

  1. Open your GitHub Pages link in Chrome on your phone.

  2. Tap the Tune / Lock icon (left of the address bar URL) or tap the 3 dots (⋮) → Settings → Site settings → All sites.

  3. Find your GitHub Pages URL and tap "Clear & reset" (or "Delete data & reset").

  4. Do not open the page yet until we update the code below.

Step 2: Make sw.js Bulletproof

Update your sw.js file with this version. It uses Promise.allSettled(), which ensures that even if an icon file is missing or 404, the service worker will not crash or freeze your app:

code JavaScript
const CACHE_NAME = 'bike-parking-v2';
const ASSETS_TO_CACHE = [
  './',
  './index.html',
  './bike_parking_lots.csv',
  './manifest.json',
  './icon-192.png',
  './icon-512.png'
];

self.addEventListener('install', (event) => {
  event.waitUntil(
    caches.open(CACHE_NAME).then((cache) => {
      // Use allSettled so missing files won't crash the install
      return Promise.allSettled(
        ASSETS_TO_CACHE.map((url) => cache.add(url))
      );
    })
  );
  self.skipWaiting();
});

self.addEventListener('activate', (event) => {
  event.waitUntil(
    caches.keys().then((keys) => {
      return Promise.all(
        keys.map((key) => {
          if (key !== CACHE_NAME) return caches.delete(key);
        })
      );
    })
  );
  self.clients.claim();
});

self.addEventListener('fetch', (event) => {
  event.respondWith(
    fetch(event.request).catch(() => caches.match(event.request))
  );
});

Step 3: Replace index.html (Native CSV Parser — No External CDN)

We can remove the external PapaParse CDN dependency and parse your CSV natively in plain JavaScript. This removes a failure point and makes the app load even faster:

  <h2>🚲 Nearest Bike Parking Lots</h2>
  <button class="btn-locate" id="locateBtn" onclick="findNearest()">Locate Nearest 5</button>
  <div id="status">Loading parking spots database...</div>

  <script>
    let parkingLots = [];
    let map = null;

    // 1. Native CSV Parser (0 dependencies, instant parsing)
    fetch('./bike_parking_lots.csv')
      .then(res => {
        if (!res.ok) throw new Error(`HTTP ${res.status}: Could not find bike_parking_lots.csv`);
        return res.text();
      })
      .then(csvText => {
        const lines = csvText.trim().split(/\r?\n/);
        const parsed = [];

        for (let i = 1; i < lines.length; i++) {
          const parts = lines[i].split(',');
          if (parts.length >= 3) {
            const name = parts[0].trim();
            const lat = parseFloat(parts[1]);
            const lng = parseFloat(parts[2]);
            if (name && !isNaN(lat) && !isNaN(lng)) {
              parsed.push({ name, lat, lng });
            }
          }
        }

        parkingLots = parsed;
        document.getElementById('status').innerText = `Ready! Loaded ${parkingLots.length} parking spots.`;
      })
      .catch(err => {
        document.getElementById('status').innerText = "Load failed: " + err.message;
      });

    // Haversine formula
    function getDistance(lat1, lon1, lat2, lon2) {
      const R = 6371e3;
      const dLat = (lat2 - lat1) * Math.PI / 180;
      const dLon = (lon2 - lon1) * Math.PI / 180;
      const a = Math.sin(dLat / 2) ** 2 +
                Math.cos(lat1 * Math.PI / 180) * Math.cos(lat2 * Math.PI / 180) *
                Math.sin(dLon / 2) ** 2;
      return R * 2 * Math.atan2(Math.sqrt(a), Math.sqrt(1 - a));
    }

    // 1-Tap Copy
    function copyCode(text, btn) {
      navigator.clipboard.writeText(text).then(() => {
        const prevText = btn.innerText;

        btn.classList.add("copied");
        setTimeout(() => {
          btn.innerText = prevText;
          btn.classList.remove("copied");
        }, 1500);
      });
    }

    function findNearest() {

        status.innerText = "Still loading parking spots database...";
        return;
      }

      status.innerText = "Acquiring GPS location...";

      navigator.geolocation.getCurrentPosition((pos) => {
        const userLat = pos.coords.latitude;
        const userLng = pos.coords.longitude;

        status.innerText = "Calculating nearest spots...";

        const withDistances = parkingLots.map(spot => ({
          ...spot,
          distance: getDistance(userLat, userLng, spot.lat, spot.lng)
        }));

        withDistances.sort((a, b) => a.distance - b.distance);
        const top5 = withDistances.slice(0, 5);

        const listDiv = document.getElementById('spotsList');
        listDiv.innerHTML = "";

        top5.forEach((spot, idx) => {
          const isFirst = idx === 0;
          const card = document.createElement('div');
          card.className = `spot-card ${isFirst ? 'closest' : ''}`;
          card.innerHTML = `
            <div class="spot-info">
              <span class="spot-rank">${isFirst ? '★ CLOSEST' : '#' + (idx + 1)}</span>
              <div class="spot-code">${spot.name}</div>
              <div class="spot-dist">${Math.round(spot.distance)} meters away</div>
            </div>
            <div class="spot-actions">
              <button class="btn-copy" onclick="copyCode('${spot.name}', this)">Copy ID</button>
              <a class="btn-nav" target="_blank" href="https://www.google.com/maps/dir/?api=1&destination=${spot.lat},${spot.lng}&travelmode=walking">Go ➔</a>
            </div>
          `;
          listDiv.appendChild(card);
        });

        document.getElementById('resultsContainer').style.display = 'block';
        document.getElementById('map').style.display = 'block';
        status.innerText = "";

        // Map rendering
        if (!map) {
          map = L.map('map');
          L.tileLayer('https://{s}.tile.openstreetmap.org/{z}/{x}/{y}.png', {
            maxZoom: 19,
            attribution: '© OpenStreetMap'
          }).addTo(map);
        }

        map.eachLayer((layer) => {
          if (layer instanceof L.Marker || layer instanceof L.CircleMarker) {
            map.removeLayer(layer);
          }
        });

        const bounds = [[userLat, userLng]];

        L.circleMarker([userLat, userLng], {
          radius: 8,
          color: '#007bff',
          fillColor: '#007bff',
          fillOpacity: 0.9
        }).addTo(map).bindPopup("<b>You are here</b>");

        top5.forEach((spot, idx) => {
          bounds.push([spot.lat, spot.lng]);
          const marker = L.marker([spot.lat, spot.lng]).addTo(map);
          marker.bindPopup(`<b>#${idx + 1}: ${spot.name}</b><br>${Math.round(spot.distance)}m away`);
          if (idx === 0) marker.openPopup();
        });

        map.fitBounds(bounds, { padding: [30, 30] });

      }, (err) => {
        status.innerText = "GPS Error: " + err.message;
      }, { enableHighAccuracy: true });
    }

    // Register Service Worker
    if ('serviceWorker' in navigator) {
      window.addEventListener('load', () => {
        navigator.serviceWorker.register('./sw.js').catch(() => {});
      });
    }

If PapaParse fails to load, Papa is undefined, causing a TypeError within the .then() block, and the .catch() doesn't seem to update the site. I am confident that a DNS or CDN issue with cdnjs.cloudflare.com is at play.

Pinpointing Failure Root

I've significantly narrowed the issue down. The fact that "Loading..." never changes strongly suggests that either fetch('./bike_parking_lots.csv') is never executed or the DOM isn't being updated, and a syntax error within the <script> block is a possible culprit. I am focusing on what may cause the code to never be reached.

Examining Potential Syntax Issues

I'm now zeroing in on a critical possibility: syntax errors. My investigation has led me to believe that a mistake within the HTML, particularly in the <script> block, is preventing the script from running entirely. I'm considering scenarios where the script may be incomplete or contain errors that halt execution before the parking lots can load, leaving the initial loading message permanently displayed. I also have to check that the CSV fetch or CDN script aren't being blocked.

Addressing Service Worker Concerns

I've just had a breakthrough! I realized I've overlooked a crucial possibility: a service worker (SW) might be interfering. If a service worker is active, it could be intercepting requests, especially if the bike_parking_lots.csv file is being cached or blocked. This is consistent with the "Loading..." message never changing. I'm now certain I need to check for a pre-existing service worker, potentially from a PWA test, and ensure it isn't the root cause. My next step is to examine the browser's application tab.

Devising Diagnostic Strategies

I am now formulating a multi-pronged diagnostic approach. First, I will look for syntax errors in index.html, and confirm the CSV loads at all. I also need to verify that a service worker is not interfering. Finally, I will check PapaParse and CDN issues. I am strongly considering offering the user an alternative index.html, which uses vanilla JS for parsing, has a visual error box, and embeds the CSV fetch with clearer feedback. A window.onerror handler will be included for immediate error display!

If you haven’t added the PWA files yet and the page is stuck at "Loading parking spots database...", it means the JavaScript encountered a silent error and stopped before the file could load.

On mobile, you can't see the developer console, so if a single character was misplaced during copy-pasting, or if the external library (PapaParse) failed to load, the page silently freezes.

The Fix

Here is a version of index.html that:

  1. Has an on-screen error catcher (window.onerror): If anything crashes, it prints the exact error in a red box on your phone screen so you aren't left guessing.

  2. Removes the external PapaParse library completely: Parses bike_parking_lots.csv using native JavaScript in 5 lines, eliminating CDN connection issues.

  3. Adds a 5-second timeout: If the CSV takes too long to load, it tells you immediately instead of staying stuck.

Replace your entire index.html on GitHub with this:

code Html
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <meta charset="UTF-8" />
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0, maximum-scale=1.0, user-scalable=no" />
  <title>Nearest Bike Parking</title>

  <!-- On-Screen Error Catcher (Displays any JS error right on your phone screen) -->
  <script>
    window.onerror = function(msg, url, line) {
      document.body.innerHTML += `
        <div style="color:#721c24;background:#f8d7da;padding:12px;margin:15px;border-radius:8px;text-align:left;font-size:13px;border:1px solid #f5c6cb;">
          <b>JavaScript Error:</b><br>${msg}<br><small>Line: ${line}</small>
        </div>`;
    };
  </script>

  <!-- Leaflet Map CSS -->
  <link rel="stylesheet" href="https://unpkg.com/leaflet@1.9.4/dist/leaflet.css" />

  <style>
    * { box-sizing: border-box; }
    body {
      font-family: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "Segoe UI", Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif;
      margin: 0; padding: 16px; background: #f4f6f8; color: #212529; text-align: center;
    }
    h2 { margin: 8px 0 16px 0; font-size: 22px; }
    .btn-locate {
      width: 100%; max-width: 450px; padding: 14px; font-size: 16px; font-weight: bold;
      border-radius: 10px; border: none; background: #007bff; color: white; cursor: pointer;
      box-shadow: 0 4px 6px rgba(0,123,255,0.25);
    }
    .btn-locate:active { transform: scale(0.98); }
    #status { margin: 12px 0; font-size: 14px; color: #666; }

    #map {
      height: 300px; width: 100%; max-width: 450px; margin: 15px auto;
      border-radius: 12px; display: none; box-shadow: 0 2px 8px rgba(0,0,0,0.1);
    }

    #resultsContainer {
      max-width: 450px; margin: 15px auto; display: none; text-align: left;
    }
    .section-title {
      font-size: 14px; font-weight: 700; color: #6c757d; text-transform: uppercase;
      letter-spacing: 0.5px; margin-bottom: 10px;
    }
    .spot-card {
      background: white; border-radius: 12px; padding: 14px 16px; margin-bottom: 10px;
      display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center;
      box-shadow: 0 2px 6px rgba(0,0,0,0.06); border: 1px solid #e9ecef;
    }
    .spot-card.closest {
      border: 2px solid #28a745; background: #fafffb;
    }
    .spot-info { flex-grow: 1; }
    .spot-rank {
      display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-weight: 700; padding: 2px 6px;
      border-radius: 4px; background: #e9ecef; color: #495057; margin-bottom: 4px;
    }
    .spot-card.closest .spot-rank {
      background: #28a745; color: white;
    }
    .spot-code {
      font-size: 20px; font-weight: 800; color: #212529; letter-spacing: 0.5px;
    }
    .spot-dist {
      font-size: 14px; color: #6c757d; font-weight: 500; margin-top: 2px;
    }
    .spot-actions {
      display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 8px; margin-left: 12px;
    }
    .btn-copy, .btn-nav {
      padding: 8px 12px; font-size: 13px; font-weight: 600; border-radius: 6px;
      border: none; cursor: pointer; text-decoration: none; text-align: center;
      display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; min-width: 80px;
    }
    .btn-copy {
      background: #6c757d; color: white; transition: background 0.2s;
    }
    .btn-copy.copied {
      background: #28a745 !important;
    }
    .btn-nav {
      background: #007bff; color: white;
    }
  </style>
</head>
<body>

  <h2>🚲 Nearest Bike Parking Lots</h2>
  <button class="btn-locate" id="locateBtn" onclick="findNearest()">Locate Nearest 5</button>
  <div id="status">Connecting to parking database...</div>

  <div id="map"></div>

  <div id="resultsContainer">
    <div class="section-title">Closest 5 Parking Spots</div>
    <div id="spotsList"></div>
  </div>

  <!-- Leaflet Map JS -->
  <script src="https://unpkg.com/leaflet@1.9.4/dist/leaflet.js"></script>

  <script>
    let parkingLots = [];
    let map = null;

    // Fetch and parse the CSV with native JS (zero external libraries)
    async function loadDatabase() {
      const status = document.getElementById('status');
      try {
        const controller = new AbortController();
        const timeoutId = setTimeout(() => controller.abort(), 6000); // 6 sec timeout

        const res = await fetch('./bike_parking_lots.csv', { signal: controller.signal });
        clearTimeout(timeoutId);

        if (!res.ok) {
          throw new Error(`HTTP ${res.status}: Could not find bike_parking_lots.csv in your repo.`);
        }

        const csvText = await res.text();
        const lines = csvText.trim().split(/\r?\n/);
        const parsed = [];

        for (let i = 1; i < lines.length; i++) {
          const line = lines[i].trim();
          if (!line) continue;
          const parts = line.split(',');
          if (parts.length >= 3) {
            const name = parts[0].trim();
            const lat = parseFloat(parts[1]);
            const lng = parseFloat(parts[2]);
            if (name && !isNaN(lat) && !isNaN(lng)) {
              parsed.push({ name, lat, lng });
            }
          }
        }

        parkingLots = parsed;
        status.innerText = `Ready! Loaded ${parkingLots.length} parking spots.`;
      } catch (err) {
        status.innerHTML = `<span style="color:#dc3545;">Failed to load CSV: ${err.message}</span>`;
      }
    }

    // Call load immediately
    loadDatabase();

    // Haversine formula
    function getDistance(lat1, lon1, lat2, lon2) {
      const R = 6371e3;
      const dLat = (lat2 - lat1) * Math.PI / 180;
      const dLon = (lon2 - lon1) * Math.PI / 180;
      const a = Math.sin(dLat / 2) ** 2 +
                Math.cos(lat1 * Math.PI / 180) * Math.cos(lat2 * Math.PI / 180) *
                Math.sin(dLon / 2) ** 2;
      return R * 2 * Math.atan2(Math.sqrt(a), Math.sqrt(1 - a));
    }

    // 1-Tap Copy
    function copyCode(text, btn) {
      navigator.clipboard.writeText(text).then(() => {
        const prevText = btn.innerText;
        btn.innerText = "Copied! ✓";
        btn.classList.add("copied");
        setTimeout(() => {
          btn.innerText = prevText;
          btn.classList.remove("copied");
        }, 1500);
      }).catch(err => {
        alert("Copy error: " + err);
      });
    }

    function findNearest() {
      const status = document.getElementById('status');

      if (parkingLots.length === 0) {
        status.innerText = "Database is not loaded yet. Check error message above.";
        return;
      }

      status.innerText = "Acquiring GPS location...";

      navigator.geolocation.getCurrentPosition((pos) => {
        const userLat = pos.coords.latitude;
        const userLng = pos.coords.longitude;

        status.innerText = "Calculating nearest spots...";

        const withDistances = parkingLots.map(spot => ({
          ...spot,
          distance: getDistance(userLat, userLng, spot.lat, spot.lng)
        }));

        withDistances.sort((a, b) => a.distance - b.distance);
        const top5 = withDistances.slice(0, 5);

        const listDiv = document.getElementById('spotsList');
        listDiv.innerHTML = "";

        top5.forEach((spot, idx) => {
          const isFirst = idx === 0;
          const card = document.createElement('div');
          card.className = `spot-card ${isFirst ? 'closest' : ''}`;
          card.innerHTML = `
            <div class="spot-info">
              <span class="spot-rank">${isFirst ? '★ CLOSEST' : '#' + (idx + 1)}</span>
              <div class="spot-code">${spot.name}</div>
              <div class="spot-dist">${Math.round(spot.distance)} meters away</div>
            </div>
            <div class="spot-actions">
              <button class="btn-copy" onclick="copyCode('${spot.name}', this)">Copy ID</button>
              <a class="btn-nav" target="_blank" href="https://www.google.com/maps/dir/?api=1&destination=${spot.lat},${spot.lng}&travelmode=walking">Go ➔</a>
            </div>
          `;
          listDiv.appendChild(card);
        });

        document.getElementById('resultsContainer').style.display = 'block';
        document.getElementById('map').style.display = 'block';
        status.innerText = "";

        // Map rendering
        if (!map) {
          map = L.map('map');
          L.tileLayer('https://{s}.tile.openstreetmap.org/{z}/{x}/{y}.png', {
            maxZoom: 19,
            attribution: '© OpenStreetMap'
          }).addTo(map);
        }

        map.eachLayer((layer) => {
          if (layer instanceof L.Marker || layer instanceof L.CircleMarker) {
            map.removeLayer(layer);
          }
        });

        const bounds = [[userLat, userLng]];

        L.circleMarker([userLat, userLng], {
          radius: 8,
          color: '#007bff',
          fillColor: '#007bff',
          fillOpacity: 0.9
        }).addTo(map).bindPopup("<b>You are here</b>");

        top5.forEach((spot, idx) => {
          bounds.push([spot.lat, spot.lng]);
          const marker = L.marker([spot.lat, spot.lng]).addTo(map);
          marker.bindPopup(`<b>#${idx + 1}: ${spot.name}</b><br>${Math.round(spot.distance)}m away`);
          if (idx === 0) marker.openPopup();
        });

        map.fitBounds(bounds, { padding: [30, 30] });

      }, (err) => {
        status.innerText = "GPS Error: " + err.message;
      }, { enableHighAccuracy: true });
    }
  </script>
</body>
</html>

Two things to verify when you update this:

  1. File name spelling: Check your GitHub repository file list and make sure your CSV file is spelled exactly bike_parking_lots.csv (all lowercase, exactly matching the code).

  2. Hard Refresh: On Android Chrome, pull down from the top to refresh so it doesn't show you a stale cached version.

Model 11:08 PM

To make your working web app installable as a native-feeling app on Android Chrome (a PWA), you just need to add 3 things to your repository without touching the core logic that already works.

Step 1: Create manifest.json

Create a file named manifest.json in your repository root:

code JSON
{
  "name": "Nearest Bike Parking",
  "short_name": "BikeQR",
  "description": "Find the nearest bicycle parking lot QR code in Singapore",
  "start_url": "./",
  "scope": "./",
  "display": "standalone",
  "background_color": "#f4f6f8",
  "theme_color": "#007bff",
  "orientation": "portrait",
  "icons": [
    {
      "src": "icon-192.png",
      "sizes": "192x192",
      "type": "image/png",
      "purpose": "any maskable"
    },
    {
      "src": "icon-512.png",
      "sizes": "512x512",
      "type": "image/png",
      "purpose": "any maskable"
    }
  ]
}

(Notice "start_url": "./" — using ./ instead of / is critical so it works inside GitHub's subfolder structure).

Step 2: Add icon-192.png and icon-512.png

Chrome on Android refuses to show the "Install" button if these two exact image sizes are missing.

  1. Go to favicon.io/emoji-favicons/bicycle/ (or generate any square image you like).

  2. Download the free zip file and unpack it.

  3. Find:

    • android-chrome-192x192.png ➔ Rename it to icon-192.png

    • android-chrome-512x512.png ➔ Rename it to icon-512.png

  4. Upload both PNG files into your GitHub repository root alongside index.html.

Step 3: Create sw.js (Fail-Safe Service Worker)

Create a file named sw.js in your repository root.

This version uses a network-first strategy so it will never freeze or block your CSV from loading:

code JavaScript
self.addEventListener('install', (event) => {
  self.skipWaiting();
});

self.addEventListener('activate', (event) => {
  event.waitUntil(self.clients.claim());
});

self.addEventListener('fetch', (event) => {
  event.respondWith(
    fetch(event.request).catch(() => caches.match(event.request))
  );
});

Step 4: Add 2 Snippets to your index.html

Open your index.html on GitHub:

1. Add this inside the <head> section (near line 7):

code Html
<!-- PWA Manifest & Colors -->
  <link rel="manifest" href="./manifest.json" />
  <meta name="theme-color" content="#007bff" />
  <link rel="apple-touch-icon" href="icon-192.png" />

2. Add this at the very bottom of your <script> tag (right before </script>):

code JavaScript
// Register Service Worker for Chrome Installability
  if ('serviceWorker' in navigator) {
    window.addEventListener('load', () => {
      navigator.serviceWorker.register('./sw.js').catch(() => {});
    });
  }

Checklist: Your GitHub Repo Files

Verify your repository has these files:

code Text
your-repo/
├── bike_parking_lots.csv
├── icon-192.png
├── icon-512.png
├── index.html
├── manifest.json
└── sw.js

How to Install it on Android

  1. Commit all files and wait ~60 seconds for GitHub Pages to finish building.

  2. Open the URL in Chrome on Android.

  3. Refresh the page once.

  4. Tap the three dots (⋮) menu in Chrome.

  5. You will now see "Install app" (or "Add to Home screen" with an install banner).

  6. Tap it, and it will be placed on your home screen with the bike icon and open in full-screen standalone mode without any browser URL bars.
